newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel museum restores man's mouldy money.
newsitem.headline: Israel museum restores man's mouldy money.

text.p: A man and his money were not parted thanks to Israeli restorers who saved the mouldy U.S. cash using methods normally employed on Picassos.
Israel Museum restorer Michael Magan said on Wednesday the unidentified man brought $20,000 in bills to him after retrieving it from its hiding place under a leaky jacuzzi.

"He said it was his mistake, that he didn't pay attention, that he thought it was a good place, under the jacuzzi," Magan told Israel Television, which showed photographs of restorers painstakingly separating bills stuck together with mould.

"In fact we saved all of it but the citizen apparently will have to pay some seven or eight percent to the Federal authorities of the bank in the United States because he didn't take good care of the money," Magan said.
He said the method used to save the cash was similar to that regularly employed on artwork, adding U.S. bills' "paper is like the paper of a Picasso print".
